title: Two-color constraints
description:
Return whether an undirected graph in adjacency-list form is bipartite, including disconnected components.

Implement `solve(...args)` and return the result; do not read stdin. Inputs are JSON values. Do not mutate inputs unless explicitly permitted.

reference.javascript: function solve(g){const c=Array(g.length).fill(-1);for(let s=0;s<g.length;s++)if(c[s]<0){c[s]=0;const q=[s];for(let i=0;i<q.length;i++)for(const v of g[q[i]]){if(c[v]<0){c[v]=c[q[i]]^1;q.push(v);}else if(c[v]===c[q[i]])return false;}}return true;}
reference.typescript: function solve(g){const c=Array(g.length).fill(-1);for(let s=0;s<g.length;s++)if(c[s]<0){c[s]=0;const q=[s];for(let i=0;i<q.length;i++)for(const v of g[q[i]]){if(c[v]<0){c[v]=c[q[i]]^1;q.push(v);}else if(c[v]===c[q[i]])return false;}}return true;}

hints: Which part of your hand-worked example repeats?
What fact from the previous step could you reuse?
Which single condition tells you a decision is safe?
editorial:
## Key insight
Every edge requires opposite colors. Restart traversal at uncolored vertices, because one successful connected component proves nothing about the rest.

## Compare approaches
Start with an exhaustive enumeration of valid candidates; it is a useful correctness oracle for small inputs, but can repeat work. The reference implementation avoids that repetition or bounds the explored states. Compare both on the smallest input and on equal values before measuring runtime.

## Complexity
Time: **O(V+E)**. Extra space: **O(V)**. Count input-dependent containers and recursion frames, not just local variables.

## Pitfalls
Check empty inputs, duplicate values, inclusive boundaries, and whether the result needs stable ordering. Passing examples alone is not proof of correctness.
